arguments.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# background_tasks.sh — runs a set of background tasks concurrently
# Usage: ./background_tasks.sh [--log-dir /path/to/logs]

set -euo pipefail

# ── Config ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
LOG_DIR="${1:-/tmp/bg_task_logs}"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"

TIMESTAMP=$(date '+%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')
SUMMARY_LOG="$LOG_DIR/summary_${TIMESTAMP}.log"

declare -a PIDS=()
declare -A PID_NAMES=()

# ── Helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
log() {
  echo "[$(date '+%H:%M:%S')] $*" | tee -a "$SUMMARY_LOG"
}

run_task() {
  local name="$1"
  local log_file="$LOG_DIR/${name}_${TIMESTAMP}.log"
  shift

  log "Starting task: $name"
  "$@" >"$log_file" 2>&1 &
  local pid=$!
  PIDS+=("$pid")
  PID_NAMES["$pid"]="$name"
  log "  → PID $pid | log: $log_file"
}

wait_all() {
  local failed=0
  for pid in "${PIDS[@]}"; do
    local name="${PID_NAMES[$pid]}"
    if wait "$pid"; then
      log "✔ Task '$name' (PID $pid) finished successfully"
    else
      log "✘ Task '$name' (PID $pid) FAILED (exit $?)"
      ((failed++)) || true
    fi
  done
  return "$failed"
}

# ── Tasks ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

task_disk_usage() {
  echo "=== Disk Usage Report ==="
  df -h
  echo ""
  echo "=== Top 10 Largest Directories under /tmp ==="
  du -sh /tmp/*/ 2>/dev/null | sort -rh | head -10 || true
}

task_system_info() {
  echo "=== System Info ==="
  uname -a
  echo ""
  echo "=== Uptime ==="
  uptime
  echo ""
  echo "=== Memory Usage ==="
  free -h 2>/dev/null || vm_stat 2>/dev/null || true
  echo ""
  echo "=== CPU Cores ==="
  nproc 2>/dev/null || sysctl -n hw.logicalcpu 2>/dev/null || true
}

task_network_check() {
  echo "=== Network Interfaces ==="
  ip addr 2>/dev/null || ifconfig 2>/dev/null || true
  echo ""
  echo "=== DNS Check ==="
  for host in google.com github.com example.com; do
    if nslookup "$host" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "  ✔ $host resolved"
    else
      echo "  ✘ $host failed"
    fi
  done
  echo ""
  echo "=== Open Listening Ports ==="
  ss -tlnp 2>/dev/null || netstat -tlnp 2>/dev/null || true
}

task_process_snapshot() {
  echo "=== Top 15 CPU-Consuming Processes ==="
  ps aux --sort=-%cpu 2>/dev/null | head -16 \
    || ps aux | sort -rk3 | head -16
  echo ""
  echo "=== Top 15 Memory-Consuming Processes ==="
  ps aux --sort=-%mem 2>/dev/null | head -16 \
    || ps aux | sort -rk4 | head -16
}

task_log_cleanup() {
  echo "=== Cleaning up old task logs (>7 days) ==="
  local count
  count=$(find "$LOG_DIR" -name "*.log" -mtime +7 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
  if [[ "$count" -gt 0 ]]; then
    find "$LOG_DIR" -name "*.log" -mtime +7 -print -delete
    echo "Deleted $count old log file(s)."
  else
    echo "No old logs to clean up."
  fi
}

# ── Main ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
main() {
  log "════════════════════════════════════════"
  log "Background task runner started"
  log "Log directory: $LOG_DIR"
  log "════════════════════════════════════════"

  # Launch all tasks in parallel
  run_task "disk_usage"        task_disk_usage
  run_task "system_info"       task_system_info
  run_task "network_check"     task_network_check
  run_task "process_snapshot"  task_process_snapshot
  run_task "log_cleanup"       task_log_cleanup

  log "All tasks launched — waiting for completion..."

  if wait_all; then
    log "════════════════════════════════════════"
    log "All tasks completed successfully ✔"
  else
    log "════════════════════════════════════════"
    log "Some tasks failed — check logs in: $LOG_DIR"
    exit 1
  fi

  log "Summary log: $SUMMARY_LOG"
}

main "$@"

content.text:
Saved to `/tmp/background_tasks.sh` and made executable. Here's what it does:

---

### What it runs (all in parallel, in the background)

| Task | What it collects |
|---|---|
| `disk_usage` | `df -h` + top 10 largest dirs under `/tmp` |
| `system_info` | kernel, uptime, memory, CPU count |
| `network_check` | interfaces, DNS resolution for 3 hosts, listening ports |
| `process_snapshot` | top 15 processes by CPU and by memory |
| `log_cleanup` | deletes task logs older than 7 days |

---

### How it works

- Each task is launched with `&` and its PID is tracked
- All tasks run **concurrently** — total wall time ≈ slowest single task
- Each task writes its own timestamped log to `/tmp/bg_task_logs/`
- After all tasks finish, `wait_all` checks exit codes and reports pass/fail
- A summary log is written alongside the individual task logs

---

### Usage

```bash
# Default log dir (/tmp/bg_task_logs)
/tmp/background_tasks.sh

# Custom log dir
/tmp/background_tasks.sh --log-dir /var/log/mytasks
```

arguments.content:
[Unit]
Description=Background Task Runner
Documentation=file:///tmp/background_tasks.sh
After=network.target network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=no

# Run as root (change User/Group if you want to drop privileges)
User=root
Group=root

# Environment
Environment=PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
Environment=LOG_DIR=/var/log/background-tasks

# Create log directory before running
ExecStartPre=/usr/bin/mkdir -p /var/log/background-tasks

# Run the script
ExecStart=/bin/bash /tmp/background_tasks.sh

# Cleanup: compress logs older than 1 day after the script exits
ExecStartPost=/bin/bash -c 'find /var/log/background-tasks -name "*.log" -mtime +1 -exec gzip -f {} \;'

# Timeouts
TimeoutStartSec=300
TimeoutStopSec=30

# Restart policy (oneshot services don't restart, but this guards accidental changes)
Restart=no

# Resource limits
Nice=10
IOSchedulingClass=best-effort
IOSchedulingPriority=7
CPUSchedulingPolicy=other

# Security hardening
NoNewPrivileges=true
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=read-only
ReadWritePaths=/var/log/background-tasks /tmp
PrivateTmp=false
PrivateDevices=true

# Output goes to journald (view with: journalctl -u background-tasks.service)
StandardOutput=journal
StandardError=journal
SyslogIdentifier=background-tasks

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

content.text: Now let's also create a timer unit so it can run on a schedule:

arguments.content:
[Unit]
Description=Run Background Tasks every 6 hours
Requires=background-tasks.service

[Timer]
# Run 2 minutes after boot, then every 6 hours
OnBootSec=2min
OnUnitActiveSec=6h

# If the timer fires while the system was off, run it immediately on next boot
Persistent=true

# Spread runs by up to 5 minutes to avoid thundering-herd on multi-host setups
RandomizedDelaySec=5min

Unit=background-tasks.service

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target

content.text:
Both files are in place. Here's a breakdown:

---

### Files created

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/etc/systemd/system/background-tasks.service` | The service unit |
| `/etc/systemd/system/background-tasks.timer` | Optional timer to run it on a schedule |

---

### Service unit highlights

**`[Unit]`**
- Starts after networking is online (`network-online.target`)

**`[Service]`**
- `Type=oneshot` — runs the script once and exits cleanly
- `ExecStartPre` — creates the log directory before running
- `ExecStart` — runs `/tmp/background_tasks.sh`
- `ExecStartPost` — compresses logs older than 1 day automatically
- `TimeoutStartSec=300` — allows up to 5 minutes to complete
- `Nice=10` / `IOSchedulingPriority=7` — runs at low priority so it doesn't hog resources

**Security hardening**
- `NoNewPrivileges=true` — no privilege escalation
- `ProtectSystem=strict` — filesystem is read-only except for declared paths
- `ProtectHome=read-only` — home dirs are protected
- `PrivateDevices=true` — no access to raw devices

---

### Usage commands

```bash
# Reload systemd after adding new units
sudo systemctl daemon-reload

# Run the service once right now
sudo systemctl start background-tasks.service

# View output/logs
sudo journalctl -u background-tasks.service -f

# Enable & start the timer (runs every 6h, 2min after boot)
sudo systemctl enable --now background-tasks.timer

# Check timer status
sudo systemctl list-timers background-tasks.timer
```

`systemctl` isn't available in this environment — this is a container without a running systemd init process, which is typical for Docker/sandbox environments.

The service file is correctly written and ready to use. On a real systemd-based host (Ubuntu, Debian, RHEL, etc.) you'd run:

```bash
# 1. Reload systemd to pick up the new unit files
sudo systemctl daemon-reload

# 2. Enable the service to start at boot
sudo systemctl enable background-tasks.service

# 3. Optionally enable the timer instead (recommended — runs every 6h)
sudo systemctl enable --now background-tasks.timer

# 4. Verify it's enabled
sudo systemctl is-enabled background-tasks.service
sudo systemctl list-timers background-tasks.timer
```

To confirm everything is wired up after running those, you can also check:

```bash
# See the full unit status
systemctl status background-tasks.service

# Run it immediately (one-shot)
sudo systemctl start background-tasks.service

# Tail the logs
sudo journalctl -u background-tasks.service -f
```

If you'd like to test the script itself right now (without systemd), it can be run directly:

```bash
bash /tmp/background_tasks.sh
```
